introH2: 🏥 What kinds of stays are near Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital, and how do you choose the right one?
introHtml: Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital sits at 133 Soi Sukhumvit 49 in Watthana — it is a JCI-accredited private hospital that draws both Thai and international patients, including many families who visit the paediatric and developmental medicine centre repeatedly over several days. The thing most people miss when booking is that the hospital is deep inside Soi 49, roughly 877 metres from BTS Phrom Phong station, so a hotel listed as being near Phrom Phong is not necessarily walkable to the hospital. The cluster of serviced apartments right on Soi 49 and Soi 49/11 are the ones that are genuinely close — and several of them run free shuttles to both the hospital and the nearest BTS. This article rounds up 6 stays in this area that we have already reviewed in depth — every pick is based on reading real guest reviews, with the genuine strengths and the honest caveats, prices compared across Agoda, Booking.com, and Trip.com, and direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital is on Soi Sukhumvit 49, about 877 metres from BTS Phrom Phong (Sukhumvit Line). Walking to the hospital from the station takes 10–15 minutes, which is why the stays deep in Soi 49 and Soi 49/11 that are the closest to the hospital all offer free shuttles to BTS as well. From BTS Phrom Phong you can reach Asok / Terminal 21 in a few stops, Siam/Siam Paragon in 3 stops, and the Airport Rail Link interchange at Phaya Thai for Suvarnabhumi Airport. The Phrom Phong–Thonglor neighbourhood around the hospital is packed with restaurants, cafés, and the Em District malls (EmQuartier, Emporium, EmSphere), reachable on foot or by a short ride.

entries.addr: 199 Soi Sukhumvit 49/11, Khlong Toei Nuea, Watthana, Bangkok
entries.storyHtml: Walton Suites Sukhumvit is a 4-star serviced suite in Soi 49/11, directly across from the entrance to Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital — just 220 metres away, a comfortable 3-minute walk without needing a taxi or motorbike. 52 units ranging from 50 to 110 sqm, every room has a full kitchen, a separate living area, a washing machine, a rooftop saltwater pool, and a free shuttle to BTS Phrom Phong and EmQuartier. Opened in 2019 and renovated in 2024, it has the most reviews in this set at 881 on Booking.com (score 8.8), with guests consistently praising the staff for helping coordinate medical appointments and navigating the hospital. Honest caveats: BTS Phrom Phong is about 987 metres away — a 12–15 minute walk in the heat, so the shuttle or Grab is needed; some reviews found a few fittings showing age despite the 2024 renovation; and lower-floor rooms can pick up street noise, so it is worth asking for a higher floor.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Let the hotel know at check-in that you are here for medical reasons — staff can help coordinate appointments and translate at the hospital. Check the shuttle timetable on day one so you can plan around it.

entries.name: Quartier by Montraj Sukhumvit
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Soi 49/11 · ~3 min walk to Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital (~200 m) · free parking

entries.storyHtml: Quartier by Montraj Sukhumvit is a 94-room boutique 4-star hotel opened in 2022 in Soi 49/11, finished in a contemporary French aesthetic — quiet, unhurried, exactly the kind of atmosphere families and patients find restful. Room sizes run from Cozy Twin (23 sqm) to Deluxe King (32 sqm); they are clean, well-maintained, and staff score an impressive 9.0 on Booking.com. The rooftop Cul de Sac bar is a genuine pleasure for an evening wind-down, and the hotel is pet-friendly with free parking. Honest caveats: there is no hotel shuttle to BTS, so every trip to the station means a Grab ride of about 10–12 minutes; the Cozy Twin and Quartier King rooms are smaller than many guests expect from a 4-star; and some reviews mention a slight musty smell in corridor areas — reporting it to staff works because they respond quickly.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Save the hotel coordinates on your phone before arrival — the entrance is tucked inside a parking area and is genuinely hard to find first time. For more space, upgrade to the Deluxe King (32 sqm).

entries.storyHtml: The LA49 Hotel is a 24-room, 3-star boutique serviced apartment in neo-classical style on Soi 49 — and with a score of 9.0 from 824 reviews on Booking.com, it carries the highest guest satisfaction in this entire set. Every room is a suite of at least 40 sqm with a separate lounge area, full kitchen, washing machine, and private balcony; many guests use the phrase "5-star service at a 3-star price" when describing the staff, who score an exceptional 9.5 on Booking.com. The hotel runs a free tuk-tuk to BTS Phrom Phong (mornings until about 1 pm) and a free shuttle between the hotel and the hospital. Honest caveats: the tuk-tuk service ends around 1 pm, so afternoon and evening trips to BTS mean a Grab (cheap at around ฿30–50); the parking area holds only about 6–7 cars and fills up on busy weekends; some rooms have a noisy air-conditioner; and a few kitchen items need to be requested ahead rather than being set out automatically.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The free tuk-tuk runs until roughly 1 pm — for afternoon or evening BTS trips, Grab is quick and very cheap (฿30–50). If you plan to cook, mention it at check-in so the kitchen is fully kitted out when you arrive.

entries.storyHtml: Adelphi Forty-Nine is a 4-star boutique serviced apartment with 86 suites, opened in 2015 — every single room is a proper suite of 50–58 sqm with a full kitchen, washing machine, private balcony, and a Japanese-style bathroom. With a Booking.com score of 9.1 (380 reviews), a staff rating of 9.4, and a cleanliness score of 9.6, it is among the best-reviewed properties in this set on a score-per-review basis. What guests mention most is the free daily shuttle to Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital and BTS Thonglor — genuinely helpful for anyone making repeated hospital visits who would rather not pay for Grab every time. Honest caveats: the hotel sits about 450 metres into Soi 49, so BTS Thonglor or Phrom Phong are a 10–15 minute walk; a few rooms face the soi and can pick up road and air-conditioning noise; and the breakfast menu is simple rather than a full buffet spread.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Tell the front desk at check-in that you need the hospital shuttle — staff will give you the daily schedule and the pick-up point. Ask for a high floor or an inward-facing room if you are a light sleeper.

entries.storyHtml: Marriott Executive Apartments Bangkok Townhall Sukhumvit is the top-tier choice in this set — a 5-star Marriott-branded serviced apartment that opened in August 2024 with 264 units, everything brand-new, scoring 8.9 from 404 reviews on Booking.com. Every unit has a full kitchen, dishwasher, washing machine, and private balcony; studios start at 43 sqm and run up to a 3-bedroom penthouse at 149–175 sqm. The hotel is on Soi 49, a straight 240-metre walk — about 3 minutes — from the hospital entrance. Reviews consistently praise the cleanliness and the condition of the rooms with phrases like "everything immaculate, nothing old." A free shuttle runs to BTS Thonglor. Honest caveats: at ฿4,200/night for a studio it is the most expensive option in this set; value improves sharply for stays of 5 days or more when the kitchen and washer earn their keep; the breakfast is described by guests as ordinary for a 5-star; and there is a per-night deposit of ฿3,000 (refunded within 14 days).
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Always book a cancellable rate when planning a medical stay — appointment dates shift. Check the free BTS Thonglor shuttle timetable on day one. For groceries, the shuttle drops at Tops Market in EmQuartier.

entries.storyHtml: Metropolis Suites Bangkok, Tapestry Collection by Hilton is the Soi 39 option for guests who want a Hilton-branded property with easy access to BTS Phrom Phong and the Em District malls. The hotel joined the Hilton Tapestry Collection in December 2024 — Tapestry is Hilton's brand for independent hotels with their own character, so this does not feel like a typical cookie-cutter Hilton. All 88 rooms are suites with a small kitchen, washing machine, and a Japanese-style toilet. A free tuk-tuk shuttle runs every 30 minutes (08:00–18:30) to BTS Phrom Phong and EmQuartier. For the hospital: Samitivej Sukhumvit is about 1.4 km away — a 6-minute motorbike taxi ride for around ฿30–40. Honest caveats: this is the lowest-scoring property in the set (Trip.com 7.9, Booking.com 7.3), reflecting a hotel in transition — some rooms still show wear and ageing fittings before the renovation programme is complete. The breakfast is a basic continental. If you ask for a renovated room at check-in you meaningfully improve your odds of a better experience.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask specifically for a renovated room when booking or at check-in. The free shuttle stops at 18:30 — for later evenings, use Grab. Motorbike taxis from the soi entrance reach Samitivej Sukhumvit in about 6 minutes.

faqTitle: FAQ — Hotels Near Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital

faq.q: Which hotels near Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital can I walk to from the hospital?
faq.a: Four properties in this set are walkable to Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital. Walton Suites Sukhumvit (220 m, ~3 min) and Quartier by Montraj Sukhumvit (~200 m, 2–3 min) are both in Soi 49/11 directly opposite the hospital. The LA49 Hotel (~280 m, ~4 min) and Marriott Executive Apartments Townhall (~240 m, ~3 min) are further along Soi 49 on the same street. Adelphi Forty-Nine (~450 m, ~6 min) is further but runs a free daily shuttle to the hospital. Metropolis Suites is on Soi 39 and needs a motorbike taxi (~6 min, ~฿35).

faq.q: Which hotels near Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital offer a free shuttle to the hospital?
faq.a: Three properties in this set run free shuttles that help with hospital access: Adelphi Forty-Nine runs a daily free shuttle directly to Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital and BTS Thonglor — the most praised free shuttle in the set. Walton Suites Sukhumvit runs a free shuttle to BTS Phrom Phong, EmQuartier, and the hospital (check schedule at front desk). The LA49 Hotel runs a free hospital shuttle and a morning tuk-tuk to BTS Phrom Phong (until about 1 pm). Always confirm the schedule with the hotel on arrival.

faq.q: Which property is best for a long stay of 1–4 weeks near Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital?
faq.a: For a stay of 1–4 weeks, the three strongest options are: Walton Suites Sukhumvit — 50–110 sqm units with full kitchens and washers, 3 minutes to the hospital; Adelphi Forty-Nine — 50–58 sqm suites with full kitchen, washer, and the Executive tier offering late check-out and laundry discounts for longer stays; and Marriott Executive Apartments Townhall — purpose-built for extended stays, brand-new in 2024, every unit has a full kitchen, dishwasher, and washer, with the value improving noticeably at 5+ nights.

faq.q: Are there family-friendly hotels near Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital with 2-bedroom options?
faq.a: Yes — several properties here have multi-bedroom options. Walton Suites Sukhumvit offers a 2-bedroom suite (75 sqm) and a Walton Suite at 110 sqm. The LA49 Hotel has a 2-bedroom suite and a 2-bedroom rooftop penthouse. Marriott Executive Apartments Townhall goes all the way to a 3-bedroom penthouse at 149–175 sqm sleeping up to 8 people — the best choice for a large family. All three have full kitchens and washing machines, which make multi-day stays considerably more comfortable.

faq.q: How do I get from Suvarnabhumi Airport or Don Mueang Airport to these hotels?
faq.a: From Suvarnabhumi Airport (BKK): take the Airport Rail Link to Phaya Thai (35 min), then BTS Sukhumvit Line to Phrom Phong station (3 stops), then a Grab or motorbike taxi into Soi 49 (5–10 min). Total time approximately 50–60 minutes. Alternatively, a taxi direct from Suvarnabhumi takes about 35–45 minutes and costs roughly ฿200–350 via the expressway. From Don Mueang Airport (DMK): a taxi takes roughly 45–60 minutes depending on traffic; or use the A1/A2 bus to Mo Chit, then BTS to Phrom Phong.

faq.q: How far is BTS Phrom Phong from Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital?
faq.a: BTS Phrom Phong station is approximately 877 metres from the hospital, which is a 10–15 minute walk in Bangkok's heat. That is why all the closest hotels in Soi 49 and Soi 49/11 offer free shuttles — walking from the BTS to the hospital every day carrying bags or managing a patient is not practical. From Phrom Phong station you can reach Asok / Terminal 21 in 2 stops, Siam in 3 stops, and transfer to the Airport Rail Link at Phaya Thai for Suvarnabhumi Airport.
